messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws Overview – State of Texas** | Topic | Key Points & Statutory Reference | |-------|----------------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• Rural interstate highways: 70‑75 mph (TX §545.001).
• Urban interstates/urban freeways: 55–65 mph depending on county.
• School zones: 25 mph during school hours (unless posted lower). | | **Seat Belt / Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts (Tx. Rev. Stat. §43.0211).
• Children under 8 years old must use approved child restraint system (CRS) appropriate for weight/height (Tx. Rev. Stat. §43.0220). | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % for drivers >21 yrs (Tx. Rev. Stat. §41.07).
• Zero tolerance for <21 yr olds (any detectable BAC).
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, possible jail time, mandatory alcohol education program. | | **Texting / Phone Use While Driving** | • Handheld phone use prohibited except when using hands-free device (Tx. Rev. Stat. §42.02).
• First offense fine up to $200; subsequent offenses higher. | | **Right-of-Way Rules** | • Yield at stop signs, red lights, crosswalks, railroad crossings, emergency vehicles, bicyclists, pedestrians.
• “Yield” sign means slow down and yield to approaching traffic. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep right lane unless passing (except on multi-lane roads where left lanes may be used for overtaking).
• Do not drive in shoulder unless stopped due to hazard. | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlamps required after sunset until sunrise, or whenever visibility ≤ 50 ft (Tx. Rev. Stat. §45.01).
• Fog lamps only allowed when fog reduces visibility below 500 ft. | | **Vehicle Equipment Standards** | • Must carry valid registration, insurance proof, driver’s license, and vehicle inspection sticker (if applicable).
• Airbag deployment requires proper installation per manufacturer instructions. | | **Parking Regulations** | • Parking on sidewalks, fire hydrants, bus stops, handicap spaces without permit is illegal.
• In residential areas, parking restrictions often marked by street signs. | | **School Bus Stop Law** | • Vehicles must stop within 20 ft of a school bus stopping to pick up/drop off children (Tx. Rev. Stat. §44.04). | | **Towing & Tow Truck Operations** | • Towed vehicles must remain stationary once secured; towing companies must follow safety protocols (Tx. Rev. Stat. §46.03). | --- ### How to Find More Detailed Information | Resource | What It Offers | Link | |----------|-----------------|------| | **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)** | Official statutes, licensing rules, forms | https://www.txdmv.gov | | **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** | Enforcement policies, DUI guidelines, accident reporting | https://dps.texas.gov | | **Texas Transportation Commission** | Highway design standards, construction codes | https://tcomm.state.tx.us | | **Texaco Legal Resources** | Summaries of major case law affecting traffic regulation | https://texacolegal.com | | **State Legislature Website** | Full text of Texas Transportation Code | https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/?link=TR | --- #### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas 1. **Always obey posted speed limits—especially near schools and hospitals.** 2. **Use hands‑free devices if you need to talk or navigate.** 3. **Keep your vehicle properly insured and registered; keep documents handy.** 4. **Check local ordinances before parking—many cities enforce strict curbside rules.** 5. **If you're new to Texas, review the *“New Driver Handbook”* available through DPS.** Feel free to let me know if you'd like deeper details on any specific area (e.g., toll road regulations, commercial truck requirements, or recent legislative changes)!
